intended_object: An edge labeling C of the complete graph on V can be pulled back along an injection f : V' ↪ V. The result is the labeling of the complete graph on V' that gives the edge {x, y} the colour C({f x, f y}). This is how a Ramsey-type colouring is restricted to an embedded vertex set. The object comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body turns the injection f into a graph homomorphism ⊤ →g ⊤. The adjacency proof works because x ≠ y implies f x ≠ f y when f is injective. It then calls the general `EdgeLabeling.pullback`, which composes C with `mapEdgeSet`. So the new labeling sends the edge s(x, y) to C s(f x, f y), which is exactly the intended restriction.

Requiring an injection is the natural condition, not a restriction. A map V' → V gives a homomorphism of complete graphs ⊤ → ⊤ exactly when it is injective, as the docstring itself explains.

This is a convenience specialisation of the general `EdgeLabeling.pullback` along graph homomorphisms, which sits in the same file. It is not a re-implementation of something available more generally, so the definition is faithful.
